# A #[foreign] mark means the same thing wherever a declaration can be
# written, not only at the top of a file. A struct declared in a component
# body is hoisted to package scope and reaches codegen the same way, so the
# mark on it and on its field has to reach codegen too.
#
# The mark used to be dropped there: the macro pass reached the document and a
# struct's body and nothing else, so the attribute wrapper survived into the
# checker — which switches over statements and matched none of its cases. The
# declaration was never registered, and the name it binds came back undefined.

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
grep 'Title:' out/index.html
! grep 'title:' out/index.html

# A component-level func carrying the mark resolves too: the symptom was the
# call site reporting the name it declares as undefined.
sngl check fn.sngl
stdout 'ok'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

component main node {
    #[foreign("js:example.com/api", "Entry")]
    struct Entry {
        #[foreign("Title")]
        title string
    }

    var e = Entry{title = "hello"}
    text(value=e.title)
}

window {
    main
}
-- fn.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

component main node {
    #[foreign("js:./api", "compute")]
    const func compute(a int, b int) => a + b

    text(value=string(compute(2, 3)))
}

window {
    main
}
